questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: A key personal safety rule in a metalwork workshop is to
options: wear loose clothing and jewellery near rotating machines
ignore machine guards when working quickly
operate machines without any prior training
wear appropriate protective clothing, such as goggles and overalls, at all times
questions.explanation: Protective clothing such as goggles, overalls, and safety boots is essential to shield workers from flying particles, sparks, and other workshop hazards.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: Machine guards fitted to workshop machinery are primarily intended to
options: prevent operators from accidental contact with moving or cutting parts
increase the speed of the machine
reduce the cost of machine maintenance
improve the appearance of the machine only
questions.explanation: Machine guards physically shield operators from moving or cutting parts, reducing the risk of serious injury during operation.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: When handling hot metal that has just been forged or heat-treated, a worker should
options: use appropriate tongs and heat-resistant gloves
ignore the temperature and proceed with bench work
handle it directly with bare hands to save time
place it immediately in a plastic container
questions.explanation: Hot metal must be handled with tongs and heat-resistant protective equipment to prevent severe burns.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: Chemicals and flammable substances in a metalwork workshop should generally be stored
options: in a properly ventilated, designated storage area away from heat sources
next to the forge or welding area for convenience
in open containers on the workshop floor
questions.explanation: Proper chemical storage in a ventilated, designated area away from ignition sources reduces the risk of fire, explosion, or harmful exposure.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: Maintaining a clean, well-organised workshop floor, free of oil spills and scattered tools, is important mainly to
options: eliminate the need for machine guards
increase the workshop's aesthetic appeal only
prevent slips, trips, and falls among workshop users
reduce the need for protective clothing
questions.explanation: A clean, organised workshop floor significantly reduces the risk of slips, trips, and falls, a common cause of workshop injuries.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: An iron-carbon alloy containing a high carbon content (typically above 2%), known for its hardness and brittleness, is called
questions.explanation: Cast iron contains a relatively high carbon content, giving it good casting properties along with characteristic hardness and brittleness.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: An iron-carbon alloy with a lower carbon content than cast iron, offering a balance of strength and ductility used widely in construction and tools, is called
questions.explanation: Carbon steel has a lower carbon content than cast iron, giving it greater ductility and toughness, useful for a wide range of tools and structures.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: Steel that has other elements, such as chromium or nickel, deliberately added to enhance specific properties is called
questions.explanation: Alloy steels have additional elements added to improve properties such as strength, hardness, or corrosion resistance beyond plain carbon steel.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: A lightweight, corrosion-resistant, non-ferrous metal widely used in aircraft and packaging is
questions.explanation: Aluminium is valued for its light weight and natural corrosion resistance, making it useful across industries from aerospace to packaging.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: A reddish-coloured, highly conductive non-ferrous metal widely used in electrical wiring is
questions.explanation: Copper's excellent electrical conductivity makes it a standard material for electrical wiring and components.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: An alloy of copper and zinc, commonly used for decorative fittings and musical instruments, is called
questions.explanation: Brass, an alloy of copper and zinc, is prized for its attractive appearance and workability, common in fittings and instruments.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: An alloy of copper and tin, historically significant and still used for bearings, bells, and sculptures, is called
questions.explanation: Bronze, an alloy of copper and tin, has been used since antiquity for its durability, and remains valued for bearings, bells, and sculptural casting.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: A bluish-white non-ferrous metal commonly used to coat (galvanise) steel for corrosion protection is
questions.explanation: Zinc is commonly applied as a protective coating (galvanising) on steel, forming a barrier against rust and corrosion.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: The heat treatment process that softens a metal, relieves internal stresses, and improves its ductility by heating and slow cooling is called
questions.explanation: Annealing softens metal and relieves internal stress by heating it to a specific temperature followed by slow, controlled cooling.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: The heat treatment process that refines a metal's grain structure by heating above its critical temperature and then air cooling is called
questions.explanation: Normalizing refines and evens out a metal's grain structure through controlled heating followed by air cooling, distinct from the slower cooling of annealing.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: The heat treatment process that increases a metal's hardness by heating it and then rapidly cooling (quenching) it is called
questions.explanation: Hardening increases a metal's hardness through heating followed by rapid quenching, though this can also make it more brittle.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: The heat treatment process performed after hardening to reduce brittleness while retaining most of the increased hardness is called
questions.explanation: Tempering follows hardening, gently reheating the metal to a lower temperature to reduce brittleness while preserving much of its hardness.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: The heat treatment process that hardens only the outer surface layer of a metal component while keeping its core softer and tougher is called
questions.explanation: Case-hardening produces a hard outer surface while retaining a tougher, more ductile core, useful for parts needing wear resistance with impact toughness.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: Ferrous metals are generally distinguished from non-ferrous metals by their
options: containing iron as a main constituent, making many of them magnetic
inability to be heat-treated in any way
complete absence of iron in their composition
questions.explanation: Ferrous metals contain iron as a primary component, which often gives them magnetic properties not found in most non-ferrous metals.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: A metallurgical process involving the extraction of a pure or usable metal from its naturally occurring ore is called
questions.explanation: Metal extraction (smelting) processes ore, typically using heat and chemical reactions, to separate and refine the usable metal.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: A measuring tool consisting of a graduated straight edge, used to measure lengths directly, is called a
questions.explanation: A steel rule is a basic graduated measuring tool used to measure straight lengths and distances directly.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: A measuring tool used to measure the internal dimensions of a hole or cavity is called an
questions.explanation: Inside calipers are specifically designed to measure internal dimensions, such as the diameter of a hole or bore.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: A measuring tool used to measure the external dimensions of an object, such as the outer diameter of a rod, is called an
questions.explanation: Outside calipers measure external dimensions, such as the outer diameter or thickness of a workpiece.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: A measuring/marking tool with one straight leg and one bent leg, used to scribe lines parallel to an edge, is called an
questions.explanation: The oddleg (jenny) caliper has one straight pointed leg and one hooked leg, allowing it to scribe a line at a set distance from an edge.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: A tool used to check or mark an accurate 90-degree angle on a workpiece is called an
questions.explanation: An engineering square provides a precise 90-degree reference edge, used to check squareness or mark right angles on a workpiece.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: A pointed hand tool used to scratch fine, accurate marking lines onto a metal surface is called a
questions.explanation: A scriber has a hardened, sharp point used to scratch precise marking-out lines onto a metal surface.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: A hand tool used to make a small indentation on a metal surface to guide the starting point of a drill bit is called a
questions.explanation: A centre punch creates a small indentation that helps prevent a drill bit from wandering off the intended starting point.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: A precisely flat, accurate reference surface used as a base for marking-out and checking flatness of workpieces is called a
questions.explanation: A surface plate provides an accurately flat reference surface, essential for precise marking-out and inspection work.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: A precision measuring tool with a sliding jaw and vernier scale, capable of measuring internal, external, and depth dimensions accurately, is called a
questions.explanation: A vernier caliper provides precise measurements of internal, external, and depth dimensions, more accurate than a simple steel rule.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: A precision measuring tool using a calibrated screw thread to measure very small dimensions with high accuracy is called a
questions.explanation: A micrometer uses a precisely calibrated screw mechanism to measure small dimensions with a very high degree of accuracy.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: A hand saw with a thin, replaceable blade, used to cut through metal, is called a
questions.explanation: A hacksaw uses a thin, toothed, replaceable blade specifically designed for cutting metal.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: The number of teeth per inch on a hacksaw blade is referred to as its
questions.explanation: Blade pitch (teeth per inch) determines the appropriate blade for different metal thicknesses; finer pitches suit thinner materials.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: A file with a flat, tapering shape used for general flat surface filing is called a
questions.explanation: A flat file has parallel, flat faces, commonly used for general filing of flat surfaces and edges.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: A file with a completely round cross-section, used for enlarging or smoothing circular holes, is called a
questions.explanation: Round files have a circular cross-section, suited to enlarging or smoothing curved or circular internal surfaces.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: A file with one flat face and one curved face, useful for both flat and concave curved surfaces, is called a
questions.explanation: The half-round file combines a flat face and a curved face, allowing it to work both flat and concave surfaces.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: A file with a triangular cross-section, useful for filing internal corners and sharpening saw teeth, is called a
questions.explanation: Triangular files have three flat faces meeting at sharp edges, ideal for internal angles and sharpening saw teeth.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: A file classified with a very fine tooth cut, used for finishing and achieving a smooth surface, is called a
questions.explanation: Smooth-cut files have very fine teeth, producing a smooth finish suitable for final surface work.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: A file classified with a coarser tooth cut than a smooth file, used for general-purpose rougher filing work, is called a
questions.explanation: Bastard-cut files have a coarser tooth pattern than smooth files, suited to faster material removal in general-purpose filing.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: A cutting tool used to cut internal (female) screw threads within a drilled hole is called a
questions.explanation: A tap cuts internal threads within a pre-drilled hole, working together with a tap wrench that turns it.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: A cutting tool used to cut external (male) screw threads onto a rod or bolt is called a
questions.explanation: A die cuts external threads onto a rod or bolt, turned using a die stock (holder).

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: The handle-type tool used to turn and apply cutting pressure to a tap when cutting internal threads is called a
questions.explanation: A tap wrench grips and turns a tap, allowing controlled cutting pressure as internal threads are formed.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: The handle-type tool used to turn and apply cutting pressure to a die when cutting external threads is called a
questions.explanation: A die stock holds and turns a die, allowing controlled cutting pressure as external threads are formed on a rod or bolt.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: The screw thread profile system based on metric (millimetre) measurements, widely used internationally, is called the
questions.explanation: The Metric thread system, based on millimetre dimensions, is the standard thread profile used across most of the world today.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: The screw thread profile system historically developed in Britain, featuring a rounded thread crest and root, is called the
questions.explanation: The Whitworth thread profile, an older British standard, features distinctively rounded crests and roots on its threads.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: The screw thread profile system standardised jointly by the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom for interchangeability is called the
questions.explanation: The Unified thread standard was jointly developed to ensure interchangeability of threaded fasteners between the US, Canada, and the UK.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: The part of a lathe machine that houses the main spindle and drive mechanism, holding and rotating the workpiece, is called the
questions.explanation: The headstock houses the spindle and drive mechanism, providing the rotational power that turns the workpiece on a lathe.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: The part of a lathe machine positioned opposite the headstock, used to support the far end of a long workpiece, is called the
questions.explanation: The tailstock, located at the opposite end from the headstock, supports the free end of long workpieces and can hold tools like drills.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: The part of a lathe machine that moves along the bed, carrying the cutting tool during a turning operation, is called the
questions.explanation: The carriage travels along the lathe bed, carrying and guiding the cutting tool as it removes material from the rotating workpiece.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: The long, precisely machined horizontal base of a lathe machine, along which the carriage and tailstock travel, is called the
questions.explanation: The lathe bed provides the accurate, rigid base along which the carriage and tailstock move during operation.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: The precisely threaded rod on a lathe machine used to drive the carriage automatically for operations such as thread cutting is called the
questions.explanation: The lead screw provides precise, synchronised movement of the carriage, essential for operations such as automatic thread cutting.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: The lathe operation that produces a flat surface at the end of a workpiece, perpendicular to its axis, is called
questions.explanation: Facing removes material from the end of a workpiece to create a flat surface perpendicular to the axis of rotation.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: The lathe operation that reduces the diameter of a workpiece uniformly along its length, producing a cylindrical surface, is called
questions.explanation: Straight (cylindrical) turning removes material evenly along a workpiece's length, producing a uniform cylindrical diameter.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: The lathe operation that produces a gradually changing diameter along the length of a workpiece, forming a cone-like shape, is called
questions.explanation: Taper turning produces a workpiece whose diameter changes gradually and uniformly along its length, forming a conical profile.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: The lathe operation that cuts completely through a workpiece to separate a finished section from the remaining stock is called
questions.explanation: Parting off uses a narrow tool to cut completely through a workpiece, separating the finished component from the remaining bar stock.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: The lathe operation that presses a diamond or straight patterned texture into a workpiece's surface, typically to improve grip, is called
questions.explanation: Knurling presses a patterned texture into a workpiece's surface, commonly used to improve grip on handles or knobs.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: Drilling machines classified as small, compact units typically mounted on a workbench are called
questions.explanation: Bench drilling machines are compact units designed to sit on a workbench, suitable for smaller drilling tasks.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: Drilling machines mounted on a tall vertical column, standing on the workshop floor, offering greater capacity than bench models, are called
questions.explanation: Pillar drilling machines are floor-standing units mounted on a tall column, offering greater size and drilling capacity than bench models.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: Drilling machines with an arm that can swing and adjust position over a large, heavy workpiece are called
questions.explanation: Radial drilling machines feature an adjustable swinging arm, allowing the drill head to be positioned precisely over large or heavy workpieces.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: A work-holding device with adjustable jaws, clamped to a drilling machine's table to securely hold a workpiece, is called a
questions.explanation: A machine vice provides secure clamping of a workpiece to the drilling machine's table, preventing movement during drilling.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: Bolts with a T-shaped head, designed to slide into the T-slots of a machine table for securing work-holding devices, are called
questions.explanation: T-bolts fit into the T-slots machined into a machine table, providing secure anchoring points for clamps and work-holding fixtures.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: The angle formed between the cutting edge of a twist drill and a plane perpendicular to its axis is called the
questions.explanation: The cutting (point) angle of a twist drill significantly influences its cutting performance and suitability for different materials.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: The angle ground onto a twist drill to prevent the heel of the drill from rubbing against the workpiece during cutting is called the
questions.explanation: The clearance angle prevents unnecessary friction between the drill's heel and the workpiece, allowing efficient cutting.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: A machine that produces flat surfaces through a reciprocating (back-and-forth) cutting motion of a single-point tool is called a
questions.explanation: A shaper uses a reciprocating single-point cutting tool moving back and forth across a stationary workpiece to produce flat surfaces.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: A machine that uses a rotating abrasive wheel to remove material and sharpen or finish tools is called a
questions.explanation: Grinding machines use a rotating abrasive wheel to remove material, sharpen cutting tools, or produce fine surface finishes.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: The process of restoring a grinding wheel's true, round shape after it has become worn unevenly is called
questions.explanation: Truing restores a grinding wheel's correct round shape and concentricity after uneven wear.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: The process of removing dull or clogged abrasive particles from a grinding wheel's surface to expose fresh, sharp grains is called
questions.explanation: Dressing removes worn or clogged abrasive material from a grinding wheel's surface, restoring its cutting effectiveness.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: Selecting an appropriate cutting speed and feed rate on a lathe is important mainly to
options: eliminate the need for any coolant or lubricant
increase the total time needed to complete a job
achieve efficient material removal while avoiding excessive tool wear or workpiece damage
guarantee the workpiece will not need further finishing
questions.explanation: Correct speed and feed settings balance efficient material removal against excessive tool wear, poor surface finish, or damage to the workpiece.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: An off-hand pedestal grinding wheel is typically used in the workshop mainly for
options: sharpening hand tools and light general-purpose grinding
questions.explanation: Pedestal grinding wheels are commonly used for sharpening hand tools such as chisels and for general light grinding tasks, rather than precision machining.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: A key safety precaution when using a pedestal grinding wheel is to
options: always use the tool rest and wear eye protection
stand directly in line with the wheel's rotation
operate the wheel with the tool rest removed
remove the wheel guard for better visibility
questions.explanation: Using the tool rest properly and wearing eye protection are essential safety practices when working on a pedestal grinding wheel, protecting against kickback and flying debris.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: A welding process using the intense heat of a burning mixture of oxygen and acetylene gas to melt and join metal is called
questions.explanation: Oxy-acetylene (gas) welding uses the flame from burning oxygen and acetylene together to melt and fuse metal at the joint.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: In gas welding, the flame setting with a balanced mixture of oxygen and acetylene, generally used for most general-purpose welding, is called a
questions.explanation: A neutral flame has a balanced oxygen-to-acetylene ratio, producing clean combustion suitable for most general welding tasks.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: In gas welding, a flame setting with excess oxygen, which can cause the weld metal to become brittle or oxidised, is called an
questions.explanation: An oxidizing flame has excess oxygen, which can lead to oxidation and brittleness in the weld metal if used inappropriately.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: In gas welding, a flame setting with excess acetylene, producing a flame with a visible feather and adding carbon to the weld pool, is called a
questions.explanation: A carburizing flame has excess acetylene, introducing carbon into the weld pool, which is sometimes desired for specific applications like hard-facing.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: A welding process using an electric arc between an electrode and the workpiece to generate the heat needed to melt and join metal is called
questions.explanation: Arc welding creates an electric arc between an electrode and the workpiece, generating intense localised heat to melt and fuse the metal.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: Personal protective equipment essential when arc welding, primarily to protect the eyes and skin from intense light and heat, includes a
options: welding helmet/shield with a darkened lens
questions.explanation: A specialised welding helmet with a darkened lens is essential to protect the welder's eyes and skin from the arc's intense light and ultraviolet radiation.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: A joint formed using a metal fastener with a rounded head on one side, hammered to form a matching rounded head on the other side, is called a
questions.explanation: A snap head rivet has a rounded head, with a matching rounded head formed on the opposite side during installation, using a snap (dolly) tool.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: A joint formed using a rivet designed to sit flush with the surface of the joined material, with a conical recessed head, is called a
questions.explanation: Countersunk rivets have a conical head that sits flush with the surface, useful where a smooth external finish is required.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: A joining method using a low-melting-point alloy, typically of lead and tin, to join metal parts without melting the base metal, is called
questions.explanation: Soft soldering uses a low-melting-point lead-tin alloy to join metal parts, without melting the base metals themselves.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: A joining method using a higher-melting-point filler metal, such as spelter, along with a flux like borax, to join metal parts at a higher temperature than soldering, is called
questions.explanation: Hard brazing uses a higher-melting-point filler metal (such as brass-based spelter) and flux like borax, producing stronger joints than soft soldering.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: A chemical substance used in soldering and brazing to clean the metal surface and prevent oxidation during heating is called a
questions.explanation: Flux cleans the metal surface and prevents oxidation during the heating process, allowing the filler metal to bond properly.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: The traditional container of glowing fuel (such as coke or coal) used to heat metal for forging is called the
questions.explanation: The hearth (forge) is where solid fuel is burned to heat metal to the high temperatures needed for forging operations.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: The heavy, flat-topped iron or steel block on which hot metal is hammered and shaped during forging is called the
questions.explanation: The anvil provides a solid, stable surface on which hot metal is hammered and shaped during forging.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: The long-handled gripping tool used to hold and manipulate hot metal safely during forging is called
questions.explanation: Tongs allow a smith to grip and manipulate hot metal safely, without direct hand contact with the heated material.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: A forging tool with a grooved surface, used to shape round or curved sections of metal, is called a
questions.explanation: A swage has a shaped, often grooved, surface used to form rounded or curved profiles in hot metal during forging.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: A forging tool with a rounded, wedge-like edge, used to spread or thin out metal at a specific point, is called a
questions.explanation: A fuller has a rounded edge used to work and thin metal at a localised point, often used before further shaping operations.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: A forging tool with a flat striking face, used to smooth and flatten the surface of hot metal after initial shaping, is called a
questions.explanation: A flatter has a flat striking face, used to smooth and finish the surface of a forged piece after its initial shaping.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: The forging operation that reduces the cross-section of a metal bar while increasing its length is called
questions.explanation: Drawing down elongates a metal bar by hammering to reduce its cross-sectional area while increasing its overall length.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: The forging operation that increases the cross-section of a metal bar at a specific point while shortening its length there is called
questions.explanation: Upsetting thickens a section of metal by compressing its length at a specific point, the opposite effect to drawing down.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: The forging operation that creates a hole through a piece of hot metal using a pointed tool is called
questions.explanation: Punching forces a pointed tool through heated metal to create a hole, often followed by drifting to refine its shape.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: The forging operation that enlarges and refines the shape of a punched hole using a shaped tool is called
questions.explanation: Drifting follows punching, using a tapered tool to enlarge and shape a hole to its final required size and profile.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: In foundry (casting) work, a full-sized model of the object to be cast, used to form the mould cavity in sand, is called a
questions.explanation: A pattern is a model, usually slightly oversized to allow for shrinkage, used to create the mould cavity in casting sand.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: In foundry (casting) work, patterns are typically made slightly larger than the finished part to allow for
options: metal shrinkage as it cools and solidifies
questions.explanation: Patterns include a shrinkage allowance because molten metal contracts as it cools and solidifies, so the pattern must be slightly larger than the final desired size.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: In sand casting, the two-part box used to contain and shape the moulding sand around the pattern is called the
questions.explanation: The moulding box (flask) holds the compacted sand in place, forming the mould cavity around the pattern before casting.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: In a two-part moulding box, the upper section is called the
questions.explanation: The cope is the upper half of a two-part sand moulding box, matched with the lower half (drag) to form the complete mould.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: In a two-part moulding box, the lower section is called the
questions.explanation: The drag is the lower half of a two-part sand moulding box, matched with the upper half (cope) to form the complete mould.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: A shaped sand form inserted into a mould to create a hollow cavity within the finished cast object is called a
questions.explanation: A core is placed within the mould to produce internal cavities or hollow sections in the finished casting, such as the bore of a pipe.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: The channel through which molten metal is poured into the mould cavity during casting is called the
questions.explanation: The gate is the channel guiding molten metal from the pouring basin into the actual mould cavity.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: A reservoir of molten metal connected to the mould cavity, designed to compensate for shrinkage as the casting solidifies, is called a
questions.explanation: A riser supplies additional molten metal to the casting as it cools, compensating for shrinkage and helping to prevent voids or defects.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: The equipment used to melt metal to a liquid state before it is poured into a prepared mould is called a
questions.explanation: A melting furnace heats metal to its liquid (molten) state, preparing it for pouring into the prepared sand mould.

questions.subject: Metal Work
questions.text: A key safety precaution during the pouring stage of foundry casting is to
options: pour the molten metal as quickly as possible with no protective equipment
allow inexperienced workers to pour without supervision
wear full protective clothing, including a face shield, against splashes of molten metal
ignore ventilation requirements in the foundry area
questions.explanation: Pouring molten metal is highly hazardous, requiring full protective clothing and equipment such as face shields to guard against splashes and burns.
